sources.title: Advice for consumers
facts: The index lists current Ofcom guidance for phone and broadband consumers
The index separates complaints, saving, switching, faults and safety guidance
limitations: An index is lineage evidence rather than proof of an individual case
Advice categories do not establish network availability

sources.title: Are you in or out of contract?
sources.geography: United Kingdom phone, broadband and pay-TV customers
facts: Providers must send end-of-contract information between 10 and 40 days before contract end
Out-of-contract customers must receive annual reminders and best-deal information
limitations: Guidance does not determine an individual contract status
Contract status does not prove service availability

sources.title: Use an Ofcom-accredited price comparison site to find the best deal
facts: The audit considers accessibility, accuracy, transparency, comprehensiveness and currency
limitations: Accreditation does not guarantee a specific deal remains available
Comparison guidance is not address-level eligibility

sources.title: Unwanted calls, texts and emails
facts: The page distinguishes nuisance marketing from scams
It covers marketing calls, spam texts, emails, silent calls and abusive calls
limitations: Guidance does not establish who sent a specific message
Reporting advice is not network-access evidence

sources.title: Types of scam calls, texts and messages
facts: The page categorises common scam-call and message patterns
The guidance focuses on attempts to obtain money or personal information
limitations: A category match does not prove fraud
Consumer-safety guidance is not parcel connectivity evidence
